title: Is DeFi Breaking After a ~$300M Hack?
description:
The DeFi ecosystem is facing a major stress test after a ~$300M hack triggered a wave of withdrawals and market instability. In this interview, Blockworks researcher Luke Ledger breaks down what happened, who’s responsible, and whether DeFi can recover.
We explore the risks behind lending protocols, the shift from monolithic to modular markets, and whether DeFi yields still justify the risk.

#DeFi #Crypto #CryptoNews #CryptoHack #Blockchain #Web3 #DeFiCrash #CryptoRisk #CryptoInvesting #Aave #YieldFarming #CryptoYield #BlockchainSecurity #CryptoMarket #CryptoAnalysis #Bitcoin #Ethereum #SmartContracts #CryptoStrategy #DeFiRisks


00:00 – Intro
 00:25 – Can DeFi Recover?
 01:12 – What Happened
 02:53 – Who Are the Hackers?
 04:58 – Who Is Responsible?
 07:47 – Monolithic vs Modular
 10:52 – Impact on Aave
 12:33 – Is DeFi Dead?
 13:02 – Yields vs Risk
 16:16 – Risk/Reward Imbalance
 17:18 – How to Stay Safe
 20:39 – Outro

They have historically accounted for close to 60% of market share in both deposits and active loans. And the result of the exploit downstream of this is a significant amount of capital has been pulled from the platform as depositors flee at the prospect of bad debt. So now these three platforms are pointing fingers at each other or at least they have been for the last couple of days. Yeah. So I'd say the nature of an exploit. It is the furthest left tail scenario, and I don't necessarily think anyone's particularly safe. That being said, by doing it on-chain, you are taking the added risk of smart contracts and counter parties. Those were very good, sensible recommendations. So thanks again for coming on our show.
